name: Persistent Combined Dystonia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Combined Dystonia

criteria.description: Presence of sustained or intermittent muscle contractions causing abnormal, often repetitive, movements and postures involving multiple body regions
Coexistence of dystonia with other movement disorders such as parkinsonism or myoclonus
Symptoms persist beyond transient or reversible causes and are chronic in nature
Exclusion of secondary causes such as drug-induced or metabolic etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of major criteria including clinical dystonia affecting multiple regions with mixed movement disorder features persisting chronically, after exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by exclusion of secondary causes and relevant investigations

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sustained dystonic posturing involving multiple body regions
searchTerms: dystonic posturing affecting multiple body parts
parkinsonism with stiffness and slow movement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intermittent myoclonic jerks superimposed on dystonia
searchTerms: myoclonic jerks on top of dystonia

common.symptomName: Cervical dystonia with abnormal neck posturing
Gait abnormalities due to dystonic involvement of lower limbs
searchTerms: gait abnormalities due to muscle spasms
difficulty walking from lower limb dystonia

occasional.symptomName: Oromandibular dystonia causing jaw opening or closing spasms
searchTerms: jaw muscle spasms causing opening or closing

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction such as orthostatic hypotension
searchTerms: autonomic nervous system problems causing low blood pressure
mood disorders including sadness and worry
emotional distress with anxiety or depression

rare.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to oculomotor involvement
searchTerms: vision problems from eye movement issues
visual disturbances due to oculomotor dysfunction
difficulty controlling eye movements affecting sight
swallowing problems leading to food entering airway

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; exclusion of metabolic and secondary causes
imaging: Brain MRI may show basal ganglia abnormalities or be normal
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with dystonia-parkinsonism syndromes (e.g., TOR1A, THAP1) may be identified
other: Electromyography showing co-contraction of antagonist muscles during dystonic movements

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated dystonia without additional movement disorder features
History of exposure to dopamine receptor blocking agents
Symptoms often reversible upon drug withdrawal

redFlags: Presence of systemic signs suggesting secondary cause
references: Albanese A, et al. Phenomenology and classification of dystonia: a consensus update. Mov Disord. 2013.
Marras C, et al. Dystonia: Clinical features and diagnosis. Neurol Clin. 2019.
Orphanet Report Series: Persistent Combined Dystonia. Orphanet. 2024.
